title: Rivergate and Provision
premise: Felix Ashgrove, a riverboat captain who has spent seven years outrunning grief by measuring life in miles, is hired to resupply an archaeological expedition upriver that has gone silent. He finds the camp abandoned except for two survivors — a wounded cartographer named Ilsa and a teenage stowaway, Dov — and evidence the team uncovered something worth killing over: proof of a pre-colonial river civilization whose artifacts a mining syndicate will destroy to keep its concession legal. Hunted by the syndicate's enforcers and racing the dry season's falling water levels, Felix must run the treacherous upper rapids at night to bring his fragile found family home. In the end he chooses to leak what the expedition found rather than stay silent, sacrificing his anonymity but finally belonging to something larger than the river.
about_author: R. M. Crane is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working cargo boats on inland waterways before writing full-time. Their fiction blends hard-won river knowledge with stories about people who build families from strangers met in dangerous places.

chapters.title: The Sound of No Answer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A routine supply contract turns strange when the expedition's radio goes quiet on schedule — too quiet, as if someone switched it off rather than lost it. Felix, who avoids attachments, almost declines the job; his late brother's voice in his memory pushes him to take it. Emotional beat: restless duty overriding self-protection.

chapters.title: Miles Instead of Years
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, interwoven with flashbacks to the accident that killed his brother seven years ago. As he loads the Rivergate with fuel, medicine, and one unexplained crate the client insisted on, we learn why he measures life in miles. Emotional beat: grief revealed as the engine of his isolation.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Two days upriver he finds signs of another boat ahead — syndicate men posing as surveyors, asking questions about the expedition. At the abandoned camp he discovers burned records, a fresh grave, and two survivors hiding in a cave: Ilsa, shot and feverish, and Dov, a fourteen-year-old stowaway clutching a satchel of stone tablets. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Map
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Feverish, she recounts what the expedition found — a terraced city predating every known culture, and how their own sponsor sold them out to the mining consortium. She entrusts Felix with her field map, drawn from memory. Emotional beat: trust extended as an act of desperation and hope.

chapters.title: Dov
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. The boy reveals he stowed away to escape a detention center, and that the syndicate's lead enforcer, Marrow, already searched him once — meaning they know the tablets exist. Felix, awkward with children, begins teaching him river-reading as a survival skill. Emotional beat: the first brittle threads of found family.

chapters.title: Downstream of Trouble
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The syndicate blocks the lower channel with a bribed lockmaster, forcing Felix toward the unmapped Serrano Rapids — runnable only at night, only at high water, and the dry season is lowering both. First chase sequence; the Rivergate takes damage. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into competence and command.

chapters.title: The Lockmaster's Price
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa, recovering, negotiates with a retired pilot who knows a backwater bypass — paying him not in money but in the truth about the city, the first time anyone tells it willingly. Meanwhile Marrow closes in, burning a friendly trading post as a message. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins to feel necessary, not optional.

chapters.title: Serrano at Night
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The night run through the rapids: Dov on the searchlight, Ilsa navigating by memory, Felix reading water by sound alone when the light dies. They survive by trusting each other completely for the first time. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into belonging — the crew becomes a family mid-catastrophe.

chapters.title: Marrow's Bargain
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cornered at the last confluence, Marrow offers Felix his old anonymous life back in exchange for the tablets and Ilsa's silence. Felix refuses, ramming the syndicate boat into the confluence shallows, and Marrow is taken by the river he exploited. Emotional beat: climax — Felix choosing people over safety, openly, for the first time in seven years.

chapters.title: Rivergate and Provision
chapters.summary: Shared POV across all three. Home past the dry-season deadline, Felix leaks Ilsa's map and photographs of the tablets to journalists and the national museum, ending the syndicate's concession. He stops measuring life in miles; Dov stays aboard as crew, Ilsa as partner. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen, family kept, justice delivered outside the law.
